S3 · Who we are

Who We Are

Equipping Boots
On The Ground

From the very beginning, HEF believed that God wanted us to raise up, support and encourage the local Haitian body of Christ to minister to the community.

God has continued to bless HEF, even amid ongoing gang violence, ensuring that our ministry has never stopped. In fact, as safety concerns grow in the larger cities, more families have moved toward the Central Plateau where we serve — leading to increased school enrollment and a greater need for food, space, teachers, and logistics.

We have been able to sustain and expand our work by equipping and empowering over 350 Haitians to serve and teach within their own communities. Thanks to our partnership with Maranatha Church, HEF has successfully grown its ministry efforts — even without sending teams from the United States.

HEF has no paid U.S. staff. It is all volunteer labor.

S4 · What we do

What We Do

Eight Ways The Work
Goes Forward

  • Support 17 churches across the Upper Central Plateau.
  • Support 13 schools, including a school for the deaf, currently serving over 3,500 students.
  • Run a feeding program serving over 3,500 hot meals daily in the schools.
  • Operate a medical ministry serving over 200 patients monthly.
    • Staff includes a full-time doctor and RN
    • Operates a clinic and pharmacy
  • Organize camps, conferences and ministries for:
    • Youth, Kids, Pastors, Women, Teachers, and Vacation Bible School (VBS)
  • Provide well drilling and solar pump installation in villages to ensure access to clean water.
  • Distribute over 3,500 Christmas gifts annually to students in the schools.
  • Care for widows and elders — 125 recipients every month.
S5 · Haiti today

Haiti Update · 2025

The Situation
On The Ground

In March and April 2025, violent attacks by criminal gangs from Port-au-Prince targeted Mirebalais and Saut-d’Eau — destroying public buildings, burning homes, and displacing tens of thousands of people.

Many displaced families sought refuge in Hinche. It remains more stable, but it is under significant strain: overcrowding, schools and public buildings occupied, infrastructure stretched past its limits.

Police forces continue resisting gang expansion into the Central Plateau, but insecurity has restricted humanitarian access and disrupted daily life. Schools and ministry activities continue in Hinche only by God’s grace.

In late November, gang leaders spoke of accepting a truce and leaving Mirebalais — a small glimmer of hope. The situation remains fragile, and we continue to pray for true peace.

Due to the safety concerns in Haiti and to protect our Haitian staff, we limit what we share publicly online. Join our prayer list to stay informed and receive the latest updates on the needs and happenings in Haiti.

S6 · 2025 in review

2025 In Review

What Your Giving Built This Year

Twelve things that happened in the Central Plateau in 2025 — in the middle of the worst insecurity in decades.

3,500 Meals A Day

The school feeding program served 3,500 hot meals every single school day.

New Well In Bohoc

Drilled a new well and installed a solar-powered water-distribution system.

20 New Classrooms

Twenty new village classrooms are under construction across the plateau.

Land In Hinche

Purchased the land next to Maranatha Church in Hinche for future expansion.

Care For The Displaced

Meals and essential care for over 450 people displaced by gang violence.

Youth Camp

Hosted more than 200 young people on our campus for a week of camp.

VBS In 8 Villages

Summer Vacation Bible School reached over 1,000 children in eight villages.

Christmas For 3,500

A school Christmas celebration — gifts and a special lunch for every student.

Women’s Learning Center

Equipping women with valuable, income-earning skills.

Widow & Elder Care

Hope and practical help delivered to 125 recipients every month.

Medical Ministry

Diagnosis, medication and surgeries for roughly 200 people a month.

Cargo Shipments

Ongoing containers of medications, Bibles, sound equipment and school supplies.

S10 · Letters

Christmas 2025

A Word From Our Leadership

As we celebrate the joy and peace of Christmas, we look back with deep gratitude for all that God has allowed HEF–Maranatha Ministry to accomplish in 2025, even amid the significant challenges facing Haiti, especially throughout the Central Plateau. Your prayers, partnership, and generosity have made every blessing possible.

The Call before us continues, even as Haiti faces worsening crisis, gang violence, and instability. Yet the Call remains as firm and compelling today as it was more than forty years ago — unchanged, unwavering, and filled with purpose.

This Christmas, we remember that the same Jesus who came as Emmanuel — God with us — is still with Haiti. May this season renew our hope and strengthen our expectation: The Call Continues. The story is far from over, and we believe the most powerful chapters of God’s work in Haiti are yet to come.

Kevin & Cindy
Haiti Endowment Fund

On behalf of all the Maranatha Churches of the Upper Central Plateau, Marie and I would like to express our deepest gratitude to all of you who, in one way or another, have supported us throughout the year 2025. Truly, we can say, “The Lord has done great things for us, and we are filled with joy.”

Thank you for your prayers, your generosity, your love, and your constant encouragement. Because of your support, our schools are well structured and well supervised. The parents and the students have received tremendous blessings, and they are very grateful.

Pastor Iliobert & Marie
Maranatha Churches, Upper Central Plateau

For 50 years, God has called and equipped us to share His love throughout Haiti. His light shines through every part of this ministry. We’re deeply thankful for our Friends of Haiti — your prayers and support help make this mission possible.
